scope: Second native performance round: batch consecutive cache-hit experts without changing quantization, arithmetic kernels, cache capacity, LRU order, dependencies, public API, or configuration.
implementation: Qwen and GLM cached single-token MoE execute consecutive cache-hit slots in one multi-expert projection/activation/down-projection batch, preserving rank output order and per-expert input stride.
Qwen grouped prefill retains its expert groups and shares a command buffer across consecutive cache-hit groups.
Every in-flight slot is pinned during the one bounded overlapping read. If the batch occupies all slots, the next read is deferred until completion.
The GPU is drained before any failed read propagates or a slot is reused; a partially read slot remains invalid.

conditions: fresh Engine per run; model/parameters fixed within cohort
one complete-request warmup per arm per model, retained and excluded from formal samples
OS file cache not purged; system load not controlled; no cold SSD or framework superiority claim
all formal samples retained; only these two inputs

prior_art.use: Existing Metal command-buffer batching; the documentation discusses balancing submission count and CPU/GPU synchronization. No new backend or dependency.

limitations: Fresh Engine per request; complete-request warmup per arm followed by A/B, B/A, A/B formal order. Only two fixed greedy inputs and context capacity 256.
OS file cache is not purged; system load is uncontrolled. All samples are retained; pooled decode steps/time is not a general quality or stable speed claim.
The old version also ran faster than in the prior round; do not compute gains by mixing rounds with different run conditions.
Larger cache runs are single exploratory requests per budget in stated order; they change memory conditions and are not code optimization gains.

The 32 GiB GLM CLI sample had a slow first half and Qwen 40 GiB had initial pauses; causes were not isolated. All slow samples remain in the report. Persistent API probes do not stream tokens to stdout and are not directly pooled with CLI samples.
No new fair framework comparison this round. The prior reference numeric result is inherited because all native logits are bitwise identical; prior reference timings are not rerun measurements.
Projection block/vector optimizations, GLM grouped projection prefill, MTP/random sampling and broader GLM long-context quality remain future work.
